subject: CloudBridge — Private egress, SDK auth, and reranker integration next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Morales <sofia@cloudbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + clarifying questions on private egress and SDK auth

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

High-level ask from CloudBridge: low-latency private connectivity for API calls (no public egress), SDK integration for structured tool-calling + embeddings-based re-ranker, and compliance evidence for our infosec review.

Key technical points we discussed (confirm if I missed anything):
- Connectivity: you want outbound requests to Redwood to traverse a VPC egress path (VPC Endpoint or NAT with controlled IP allowlist) and avoid any public, dynamic egress IP.
- Auth: preference for short-lived mTLS certs or customer-managed API keys (you said you have an internal cert rotation process).
- SDK: plan to use Redwood SDK to call structured outputs and tool-calling. Need example JSON schema for structured output + SDK call pattern.
- Embeddings & rerank: want to push candidates to a reranker pipeline in Redwood (embeddings + rerank step) and understand tokenization/embedding model options and associated latency/cost tradeoffs.

Immediate deliverables we can provide by Friday:
1) A short network sketch with recommended VPC endpoint vs. IP allowlist options (attachment: cb-network-sketch-v1.png).
2) An SDK snippet for structured tool-calling + sample response schema.
3) Answers to your MATP/compliance checklist (attachment: CloudBridge_MATP-answers.pdf).

Questions for your team: 
- Which connectivity mode do you prefer to evaluate first: a Redwood-managed VPC Endpoint (we stand up a peered endpoint and advertise static egress IP) OR an IP allowlist on your egress NAT (you provide the NAT IPs)?
- For mTLS: do you require mutual TLS where CloudBridge presents a client cert, or would short-lived API tokens (rotated by your secrets manager) be acceptable?
- Expected request volume/peak RPS and typical prompt length for the reranker flow (this will guide model/quantization suggestions).

Next steps: I’ll attach the network sketch and the SDK example in a follow-up; if you’re good we can schedule a short technical session with our Solutions Engineer (Karthik) to walk the team through mTLS and VPC endpoint setup.

Best,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + clarifying questions on private egress and SDK auth

Thanks Ben — great summary. A few clarifications and answers from CloudBridge: 

1) Connectivity preference: we prefer the VPC Endpoint approach first (gives our security team the deterministic path they like). We still need to understand DNS routing (will DNS resolve to a private IP inside our VPC?) and whether the endpoint supports regional failover.

2) mTLS vs API tokens: security wants mTLS as the primary — they currently have an internal CA and cert-rotation pipeline (HashiVault). Can Redwood accept client certs signed by a customer-managed CA? If not, we can explore short-lived cert issuance via a delegated PKI.

3) Volume: initial pilot ~20 RPS peak, average prompt ~180 tokens; reranker receives ~6 candidates per query. If latency delta between a heavy reranker and lightweight reranker is >70ms we may evaluate batching.

4) Compliance pack: thanks for the MATP answers; please include example audit log entries showing request IDs that include customer_project ids for traceability.

We attached a redlined network diagram internally — will share after the technical session. Two quick asks before the call with your SREs: 
- Can Redwood provide a sample mTLS client cert validation flow (server-side verification steps)?
- Example SDK structured-output payloads for a tool-calling rerank + embed step.

Happy to meet next Tue or Wed morning PT.

—Sofia
Head of Platform Integrations
CloudBridge

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + clarifying questions on private egress and SDK auth

Sofia — great, VPC endpoint first works. A few concrete notes inline and an attached SDK snippet Ill also drop into the Drive folder: 

- DNS: Redwood supports a private endpoint that resolves to an internal VPC IP (we provide a Route53 private hosted zone entry that you can import, or you can configure conditional forwarding to our endpoint). Regional failover: we can advertise multiple endpoint IPs; failover is supported within the same region.

- mTLS: we do accept customer-signed client certs. The server-side validation steps we support: 
  * Validate client cert chain against provided CA bundle
  * Check OCSP/CRL status if you publish revocation lists
  * Verify cert SAN matches project identifier (we can apply SAN naming policy)

- SDK structured-output snippet: attached gist shows how to call the tool-calling API and a sample JSON schema for the reranker output (score + chosen_id). We will include an example that demonstrates embedding calls followed by a rerank request (two RPCs in the sample).

Action items Im assigning now: 
- Ben: produce SDK snippets + example payloads and upload to Drive (ETA: EOD Thu).
- Karthik: schedule a 60-min technical session with CloudBridge SREs to walk through endpoint provisioning, TLS certs, and NAT fallback options (ETA: propose slots).
- CloudBridge (Sofia): confirm which VPC (us-west-2) you want to peer to and share the CIDR and desired SAN naming convention for certs.

If helpful, we can prepare two configuration templates during the session: (A) VPC endpoint with Route53 private zone; (B) NAT egress + static IP allowlist with DNS rewrite.

Ben

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + clarifying questions on private egress and SDK auth

Looping in a few implementation details and next steps from the engineering side — summarized plan and owners.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Provision private endpoint (Redwood): create a Regional Private Endpoint in us-west-2 and provide a Route53 private hosted-zone record. CloudBridge to accept peering and inject the private zone. (Owner: Redwood SRE / Karthik)
2) mTLS client certs: CloudBridge will provide the CA bundle and desired SAN policy. Redwood will configure server-side verification and publish the validation logs to your audit project. (Owner: CloudBridge + Redwood Security)
3) SDK integration: provide two SDK patterns — (a) direct tool-calling with structured JSON schema and (b) split flow: embeddings -> candidate scorer -> reranker. Include code for token counting and batching knobs. (Owner: Ben)
4) Fallback: NAT-based static IP allowlist option as a backup for initial testing. We'll provide the static egress IPs if the VPC peering has delays. (Owner: Redwood Infra)

Pre-call checklist for next week (technical session):
- CloudBridge: share VPC CIDR and desired SAN naming rule (by Mon 11/22).
- Redwood: upload SDK snippets + example reranker payloads to the Drive folder and invite CloudBridge SREs (Ben, ETA: EOD Thu 11/19 — done).
- Security: confirm audit-log format (we will emit request_id, project_id, model, latency_ms, outcome).

Delivery timeline (proposed):
- Week of 11/22: technical session and endpoint provisioning kickoff.
- Week of 11/29: pilot traffic (20 RPS) to VPC endpoint; telemetry review.

Open questions for CloudBridge: 
- Cert rotation frequency: how often do you rotate client certs (daily/weekly/monthly)? Well validate the refresh window for mTLS sessions.
- Rerank batch sizing: do you want us to recommend batching heuristics based on 6 candidates / 180-token prompts, or simulate expected latency with our perf profiler?

Lauren — can you review the commercial implications of offering a dedicated regional endpoint for a pilot (small uplift)? Well surface the proposed uplift in the commercial thread.

Thanks — Ill propose 3 slots for next Tue/Wed for the technical session in a separate calendar invite.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
